_about: T2 package vectors. Each entry is a frozen .treeship package under this directory and the verdict each verifier must give it. cli* columns are the `verdict` field of `treeship package verify --format json` (run.sh); receipt_only is the core-wasm verify_receipt outcome, which @treeship/verify's verifyReceipt returns (packages/core/tests/package_vectors.rs). xfail maps a column to {task, got}: the fix-plan task that makes it right and the exact wrong verdict main gives today; remove the entry in that task's PR. Every new advisory adds a vector.

honest/approval._note: CLI-18 / W1-13: on a second ship that pinned the producer, --strict verifies: the unchained approval is bound by the chained action's signed approvalNonce, and the producer's journal row is not applicable there

honest/endorse-non-latest._note: CLI-1: an endorsement of an older artifact, with an action chained onto it; the endorsement signs its parentId (0.31.10+)

honest/legacy-0.24._note: built by 0.24.0, before packages carried envelopes (0.31.2): default and strict fail by design, --structural is the documented path

honest/legacy-endorsement-0.31.9._note: the same flow written by treeship 0.31.9, whose endorsements sign no parent: chain_linkage warns (compatibility path), --strict promotes it to a failure

honest/room-countersigned._note: CLI-3 + W1-13: invite, join, host-minted challenge, countersign, close on one ship. The invitation, participant and liveness record are unchained but bound by signed references, so --strict verifies with the host pinned

tampered/approval-evidence-deleted._note: Round 3 (embargoed): honest/approval with approvals/ deleted; the close record still binds receipt.json, and approval_evidence fails because the consuming action has no use record

tampered/approval-max-uses-raised._note: Round 4 (embargoed): honest/approval with a second use record for the single-use approval, and max_uses raised to 99 on the (unsigned) use records with their digests recomputed. replay-package-local trusts the record's max_uses and passes; approval-use-limit reads the approval's signed scope and fails; --structural fails it too (approval-use-chain-continuity: the added record is not anchored)

tampered/approvals-share-a-nonce._note: Round 5 (embargoed): two sealed approvals share one nonce (the approver's single-use one and an unbounded one signed by the producer); two actions consume it. approval-use-limit fails on the shared nonce approval-use-limit judges the signed scope under --structural too (a forged or over-used grant is a failure of the bytes, whatever the reader trusts).

tampered/carried-grant-overused._note: Round 5 (embargoed): a single-use approval minted before the session is carried only in approvals/grants, and two sealed actions consume it; its signed limit applies exactly as for a sealed approval approval-use-limit judges the signed scope under --structural too (a forged or over-used grant is a failure of the bytes, whatever the reader trusts).

tampered/drop-record-json._note: CLI-4: the signed close record is deleted; the package still carries envelopes and a coverage receipt, so it cannot be pre-0.31.4

tampered/drop-record-json+rename._note: CLI-4: close record deleted, then session.name edited

tampered/empty-package._note: H2 (embargoed): a package that seals no artifacts and carries no close record. 0.31.9 rates it verified by default: nothing failed

tampered/endorsement-parent-edited._note: honest/endorse-non-latest with the endorsement's signed parentId pointed at its subject: a present parentId never falls back to the legacy path

tampered/forged-close-record._note: H1 (embargoed): honest/basic with receipt.json rewritten, an attacker key added to keys.json, and a fresh session.v1 record signed by it over the new digest. 0.31.9 rates it verified under --strict with the producer pinned

tampered/forged-record-pinned-other-key._note: Bypass E (embargoed): honest/basic rewritten and re-bound by a record signed by a second key the reader has also pinned (cli_strict pins every key in keys.json, producer and the second key). A pinned key must not vouch for another session's receipt

tampered/injected-signer-artifact._note: Bypass B (embargoed): honest/basic with an attacker-signed action chained in (tree recomputed), receipt rewritten and a record by the attacker key; cli_strict pins only the producer; --structural runs after the strict pass has pinned the producer, so signer_trust fails there too (a pinned package carrying an unvouched signer)

tampered/key-id-reused-by-forger._note: Round 3 (embargoed): honest/basic re-signed end to end by a forger's key under the victim's key id, narrative edited. The reader pinned the victim (cli_strict and cli_pinned pin honest/basic's key under that id): key_id_collision fails it. With nothing pinned it is indistinguishable from any unknown signer's package, so the unpinned cli column may accept
tampered/key-id-reused-by-forger.unpinned_indistinguishable: a forger's own package under an unpinned key

tampered/lone-attacker-close._note: a2 (embargoed, round-2 review): as E4 with the attacker key unpinned and nothing pinned; round 1 rated it signatures-pass

tampered/room-countersign-stripped._note: honest/room-countersigned with the host countersign removed from the sealed participant

tampered/room-double-redemption._note: #483 review: one single-use invitation, two participants, both countersigned by the host through the CLI (the second joiner's pending envelope copied into the host store). The second participant row fails: redeemed 2 times, max_uses 1

tampered/room-invitation-dropped._note: honest/room-countersigned with the invitation envelope removed: the participant fails, it never falls back to the generic signature check

tampered/room-participant-sealed-twice._note: #483 review: honest/room-countersigned with its participant listed twice and the tree recomputed; the duplicate row fails (and receipt_binding, since the record no longer binds the receipt)

tampered/second-close-by-pinned-key._note: E4 (embargoed, round-2 review): a key the reader pins (cli_strict pins every key in keys.json) appends its own chained session.close for this session and signs a record naming it; round 1 rated it verified

tampered/smuggled-approval._note: W1-13 condition 1a: honest/approval plus an unchained approval and a chained action consuming its nonce, both signed by a key nobody pinned (tree recomputed with splice.py, record kept). The attacker's own action cannot bind the smuggled approval; cli_strict pins only the producer; --structural runs after the strict pass pinned the producer, so the unvouched signer fails signer_trust there too

tampered/splice-action._note: CLI-4 (#474 security review): session 2's action, signed by the same key with parentId = session 1's last chained artifact, appended to session 1's package with the tree recomputed and record.json deleted. 0.31.9 rates it verified

tampered/splice-action-record-kept._note: as splice-action with record.json kept: receipt_binding fails because the sealed set no longer digests to what the close record signed

tampered/splice-handoff._note: as splice-action, with a handoff whose artifacts[0] names session 1's last chained artifact
